newsitem.title: USA: Republicans seek to stop Democratic spending.
newsitem.headline: Republicans seek to stop Democratic spending.

text.p: The Republican Party will ask a federal court for an injunction to stop the Democratic Party from further spending until it files its financial report with the Federal Election Commission, Republican Party Chairman Haley Barbour said on Tuesday.
Barbour announced the court action after the Democratic party failed to file with the FEC details of spending and contributions that were due last Thursday.

"To make sure the law is in force, the Republican National Committee will file a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia seeking a temporary restraining order that would freeze all Democratic National Committee (DNC) assets and prevent the DNC from expending any funds (on the election) until the FEC report is filed as required by law," Barbour said in a statement.
Democrats scrambled to limit the damage of the controversy, with party chairman Sen. Christopher Dodd promising that documents on campaign contributions would be released.
"We're not holding back. Every document, whatever has to be complied with, will be available as fast as it could be," Dodd said in Boston.
The dispute follows reports of donations to the Democratic party from Taiwan and Indonesia and questions whether the foreign money influenced policy in the administration of President Bill Clinton.
